tools.name: tokvera
tools.compat_warning: tokvera v0.1.0-dev is outside the versions this release supports (>=0.2.0 <0.3.0)

top.title: Hard-coded Slack token
top.fix: Move it to the environment or a secret store and reference it (for example ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}); then rotate it, since it has been on disk.
top.detail: A credential is written in the configuration file, readable by anything that can read the file and copied into backups and dotfile repositories.

top.title: Literal value in secret-named field X-API-Key
top.why: deal risk: a customer security review would flag Sievant SEC002 (high)
top.fix: Reference it from the environment (for example ${X_API_KEY}) and rotate it.
top.detail: The field's name says it holds a credential, and its value is written in the file rather than referenced.

top.title: Credential embedded in the server URL
top.why: deal risk: a customer security review would flag Sievant SEC004 (high)
top.fix: Rotate the URL with the provider if it has been shared, keep the file private, and prefer a provider option that authenticates with a header referenced from the environment.
top.detail: The URL itself grants access (path segment 2 (high-entropy)). Anyone who sees it can use the server: it is copied into logs, process lists, shell history, screenshots and support tickets.

top.title: Credential embedded in the server URL
top.why: deal risk: a customer security review would flag Sievant SEC004 (high)
top.fix: Rotate the URL with the provider if it has been shared, keep the file private, and prefer a provider option that authenticates with a header referenced from the environment.
top.detail: The URL itself grants access (query api_key (token query key)). Anyone who sees it can use the server: it is copied into logs, process lists, shell history, screenshots and support tickets.

top.title: Requests are failing
top.why: Tokvera fail on latency, impact 30 grade points (at or above the median 30)
top.why_it_matters: Every failed request is either a user-visible error or a retry that costs latency and money. The status breakdown in the evidence says whether it is rate limiting, timeouts or server errors.
top.fix: For 429s, raise the rate limit or add client-side retry with exponential backoff and jitter. For timeouts, compare the request timeout with the measured request duration. For 5xx, read the server logs at the times of the scan.

findings.title: Requests are failing
findings.why: Tokvera fail on latency, impact 30 grade points (at or above the median 30)
findings.why_it_matters: Every failed request is either a user-visible error or a retry that costs latency and money. The status breakdown in the evidence says whether it is rate limiting, timeouts or server errors.
findings.fix: For 429s, raise the rate limit or add client-side retry with exponential backoff and jitter. For timeouts, compare the request timeout with the measured request duration. For 5xx, read the server logs at the times of the scan.

findings.title: Failures rise at the highest concurrency
findings.why: Tokvera fail on latency, impact 30 grade points (at or above the median 30)
findings.why_it_matters: The endpoint refuses or drops requests once enough arrive together, which is exactly when traffic peaks.
findings.fix: Size capacity or rate limits for the concurrency your traffic reaches, and make the client back off on 429 and 503 rather than retrying immediately.

findings.title: No Prometheus metrics at /metrics
findings.why: Tokvera warning on operational, impact 5 grade points
findings.evidence: no Prometheus exposition answered at /metrics on the target's origin
findings.why_it_matters: Queue depth, batch size and cache usage are what explain a latency problem. Without them, a slowdown can be seen but not diagnosed.
findings.fix: Enable the server's metrics endpoint (llama.cpp needs `--metrics`; vLLM and TGI serve /metrics by default) and scrape it. If the endpoint sits behind a gateway, expose the metrics there.

privacy: Tokvera contacts only the target you specify, plus GitHub when you run update or doctor --check-update, and tokvera.halotrcer.com and GitHub for the plugin's first-run install.
The load used Tokvera's fixed, harmless benchmark prompts. Response text was read for timing and discarded; none is stored in this report.

findings.title: Server runs with all permissions (Deno)
findings.fix: Grant only the access the server needs (for Deno, --allow-net=<hosts>; for containers, a dedicated network).
findings.detail: The server can reach far more than its tools need, which widens what a compromised or manipulated server can do.

notes: Tool descriptions, and the resources and prompts each server offers, were not checked: that needs starting the servers (sievant scan --inspect-tools, which runs them).

gaps.title: No audit trail to report on
gaps.fix: Run Sievant (sievant proxy through sievant wrap, or sievant serve) so it records calls, and point --audit at its store.

gaps.title: Wrapped servers allow every tool
gaps.fix: Write a configuration (sievant init --profile balanced or strict), let it observe, then narrow it with sievant policy suggest and apply.

gaps.title: Suspected prompt injection is recorded, not acted on
gaps.fix: Set injection.action to annotate (the injection pack) or block for the agents that need it.

gaps.title: Personal data in tool arguments is passed on
gaps.fix: Set sanitization.input_pii to redact or block (pack secrets-pii).

gaps.title: MCP client configurations were not checked
gaps.fix: Run sievant report without --no-clients, or sievant scan.

gateway.disclaimer: This report describes how Sievant is configured and what its audit trail recorded in the period. It is generated by the software from local data; it is not a certification, an audit or an attestation, and it covers only the MCP traffic that passes through Sievant.

privacy: Halotrcer contacts only the target you give it (through Tokvera) and reads only the MCP configuration files Sievant reads, on this machine. It sends no telemetry. Secrets stay masked as each tool masks them; on top of that, Halotrcer drops URL credentials and query strings, hides environment values, shows your home directory as ~ and replaces your user name with <user>.
